deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a natural-philosophical argument from Riemann's philosophical Nachlass about teleology (Zweckmässigkeit) and the hypothesis of an 'Erdseele' (earth-soul). The next page names Fechner explicitly, so this engages Fechner's Zend-Avesta. The logical structure of the page is as follows.

(P1) Causal principle for purposiveness. Any particular purposiveness, i.e. one occurring within a bounded domain of phenomena, must have a cause bounded in time and space. General purposes are explained by an eternal Willing that is not produced in any temporal process. Riemann corrected 'unbedingte' (unconditioned) to 'allgemeine' (general).

(P2) Epistemic premise. The only purposiveness whose cause we perceive directly is that of our own actions, and that cause is our thinking. The sentence breaks off after 'd.h.'.

(P3) Hence for every purposiveness we perceive, we can only seek its cause in a thinking process (Denkprozess). We have no other mode of explanation.

(R) Rule of inference. Suppose a material body shows a closed system of mutually interlocking, variable, continuing relations of purpose and effect. Then the most probable explanation is a continuing, unified thinking process within that body, provided two conditions hold:
- (C1) the purposiveness does not split into several particular purposivenesses that are already complete within parts of the body; and
- (C2) there is no reason to seek its cause in a larger whole to which the body belongs.
Schematically: closed system & C1 & C2 => (most probable) a unified mind in the body.

(A) Application to humans, animals and plants. Part of the observed purposiveness is explained by a thinking process inside these bodies. The other part, the purposiveness of the organism's own structure, is explained by a thinking process in a larger whole. Three reasons are given, each showing that C2 or the continuity requirement fails for organic structure:
1. Organic arrangements do not reach closure in the individual organism. The reasons for the human organism's design lie in the constitution of the whole earth's surface, organic nature included. So C2 fails.
2. Organic movements recur countlessly, side by side in different individuals and one after another in the life of an individual or a lineage. So a common cause, not a separate one in each case, must be assumed.
3. Organic arrangements undergo no further development during the life of the individual (humans, animals) or of the single lineage (plants and the lower forms). So their cause is not a simultaneously running thinking process inside them.

On the next page Riemann concludes that, after removing organic purposiveness, a closed system remains in humans and animals (and in plants on Fechner's view), explained by an inner unified mental principle. Applying the same rule (C1, C2, plus progressive development) to the whole earth yields the Erdseele as a hypothesis of exact natural science.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics.

Philosophically, the step from P2 to P3 is a strong inductive extrapolation: the only cause of purposiveness we know is thought, therefore all purposiveness has thought as its cause. Riemann flags this himself ('eine andere Erklärungsart haben wir nicht').

Point 3 assumes organic structure does not develop within a lineage ('im Leben der einzelnen Geschlechter keine Fortbildung'). This is a pre-Darwinian or Darwin-neutral assumption, while the next page invokes progressive appearance of more perfect organisms over the earth's life.
The sentence 'Diese Ursache ist unser Denken d.h.' is left unfinished in the manuscript.

results.what: Teleological inference rule: a closed system of purpose-effect relations in a body, not decomposable into parts and not referable to a larger whole, is most probably explained by a unified inner thinking process; applied to organisms and, on the next page, to the earth (Erdseele).
results.modern_name: Argument from design / inference to the best explanation for panpsychist 'world-soul' hypotheses (Fechner's Erdseele)
results.usually_credited_to: G. T. Fechner (Zend-Avesta, 1851; Nanna, 1848), building on Kant's Critique of Judgment on teleology

deep.surprise_reason: This is a purely philosophical page. Riemann's sympathy for Fechner's psychophysics and earth-soul hypothesis is well documented: Dedekind/Weber printed 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts' including 'Naturphilosophie' and remarks on Fechner in the Gesammelte Werke (1876). This passage appears to belong to that known material or is very close to it. There is no mathematical content.

checkable.sympy: from sympy.logic.boolalg import Implies, And, Not; from sympy import symbols; from sympy.logic.inference import satisfiable; S,C1,C2,M=symbols('S C1 C2 M'); satisfiable(And(Implies(And(S,C1,C2),M), S, C1, Not(C2), Not(M)))
checkable.asserts: The rule (closed system & C1 & C2 => inner mind) is consistent with a case where C2 fails (organic structure points to a larger whole) and no inner mind is inferred. This only illustrates that the page's inference about organic structure rests on the failure of C2, not on a contradiction.

transcription_corrections: Line 7: the manuscript reads 'Diese Ursache ist unser Denken d.h.', with 'Diese Ursache' written above a struck 'Sie'. The sentence is unfinished in the original, not a transcription gap.
In 'Für die Zweckmäßigkeit, welche in ihnen sich [?] zeigt', the illegible word may be 'schon' ('sich schon zeigt'); uncertain.
'(bei Pflanzen und Pflanzenthieren[?])': the image is unclear and could read 'Thierkolonien' or 'Thierpflanzen' (zoophytes); 'Pflanzenthieren' is plausible but uncertain.
Point numbering: the manuscript writes '1,' '2,' '3.' with mixed punctuation; the second item in the 'Gründe' list is written with a large '2,' that resembles 'B,'.
